clue.text: Johnny discussed fish platter from the 1960s

definitions.note: a platter is an old word for a gramophone record; this one is a 1965 Beatles album

parts.note: British slang: a johnny, or rubber johnny, is a condom, also called a rubber

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so the fish is taken by its sound

parts.note: the sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Someone called Johnny talked about a fish dish served back in the sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platter' looks like a serving dish to go with the fish, but it is slang for a vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber Soul is the Beatles album released in 1965, and records were once nicknamed platters.

clue.text: When making arrival, Scottish songstress worked up screech

indicators.note: in a down clue, worked up means the letters run upwards, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: ETA, estimated time of arrival, tells you when someone arrives
Lulu is the Glasgow-born pop singer

explanation.surface: A Scottish singer, on arriving, got herself so agitated that she screamed.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer famous for 'Shout'. The whole combination is read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to howl or wail in a high trilling voice, a kind of screech.

clue.text: Showy bee hives?

parts.note: the letter B is spelt bee
hives is an itchy skin rash

explanation.surface: A question about whether beehives are ostentatious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hives' looks like the bees' homes, but here it is the skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means loud and self-assertive, flashy in a vulgar way.

clue.text: Dieter's drink, with calories halved, Heather wanted

indicators.note: calories loses half its letters, the front four, keeping only the back half

parts.note: ling is the common heather

explanation.surface: Someone on a diet wants a drink with half the calories, and Heather wants one too.
explanation.walkthrough: Dieter is a German man's name, so his drink is a German wine; the slimmer is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is the classic German white wine grape and wine, fitting a German called Dieter.

clue.text: Some poetry concert hall presented with humour once?

parts.note: an odeon was a building for musical performance in ancient Greece, and the name of a cinema chain
melancholy, black bile, was one of the four humours of old medicine

explanation.surface: A concert venue staging a comedy show of old-fashioned humour.
explanation.walkthrough: Medieval medicine held that four humours governed temperament; 'humour' here is not comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ode on Melancholy is one of Keats's great odes of 1819, a well-known piece of verse.

clue.text: Olympic venue to continue constructing pool

parts.note: Los Angeles hosted the Olympics in 1932, 1984 and will again in 2028
to go on is to continue

explanation.surface: An Olympic host city carries on building a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of still water cut off from the sea, a natural pool.

clue.text: Do outside portrait finally when in charge

indicators.note: the last letter is placed in the middle of the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: only the last letter of portrait is used

parts.note: the word whose final letter is used

explanation.surface: Instructions for having a portrait done outdoors while you are in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do outside' reads as an instruction, but it means an outdoor party; 'in charge' is split across two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a garden party or open-air fair, a social do held outdoors.

clue.text: Shake salt over small snacks?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the next

parts.note: to flap is to wave or shake to and fro
an old salt and a jack (jack tar) are both sailors

explanation.surface: A cook is told to sprinkle salt over little nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is a sailor, as in old salt; a flapjack is a British oat bar, the question mark covering the word's other sense of pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: Flapjacks are chewy baked oat bars eaten as snacks in Britain.

clue.text: Hazel perhaps embracing Malcolm regularly avoided sentimentality

indicators.note: the tree's letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: hazel is an example of a tree

indicators.note: every other letter of Malcolm is skipped, keeping the alternate ones

parts.note: the name supplies its second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A woman called Hazel hugged Malcolm but steered clear of getting soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel and Malcolm look like a couple; Hazel is the tree, and Malcolm only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is used figuratively for cloying, syrupy sentiment, just as syrup is.

clue.text: Country's graduate element switching sides

indicators.note: the two pieces given in the clue trade places, so element comes first

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A nation's college graduate changes political allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the Caribbean island nation.

clue.text: Always pleased to vacate enormous habitat of alligators

parts.note: ever means always
glad means pleased

indicators.note: enormous is emptied of its inner letters, leaving its ends

parts.note: the word whose first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A huge wildlife home that is always happy to be moved out of.
explanation.definitionFit: The Everglades are the subtropical Florida wetlands famed for their alligators.

clue.text: Factory worker battles house rules, essentially

parts.note: war is a state of armed battles

indicators.note: the essence, the heart, of rules is its middle letter

parts.note: the five-letter word whose central letter is used

explanation.surface: A factory employee fights over the essential house rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The Factory was Andy Warhol's New York studio, so the 'worker' is the artist himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol ran his art studio, called The Factory, in 1960s New York.

clue.text: Beginner finding speed of light in plane doable?

definitions.note: the phrase is adjectival, as in 'money is no object', meaning not a barrier

parts.note: noob is slang for a newcomer, especially in gaming

indicators.note: the symbol is placed inside the plane

parts.note: a jet is a jet-engined aeroplane
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A novice wonders whether light-speed travel in an aircraft is feasible.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose, hence the question mark: if cost is no object, it is doable.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is no object means it is no obstacle, so the thing can be done.

clue.text: Slate fragment on shelter

indicators.note: in an across clue the fragment is placed after the shelter

parts.note: a den is an animal's shelter
an ounce is a tiny amount, as in 'not an ounce of sense'

explanation.surface: A broken piece of roofing slate lying on a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slate' looks like a roofing tile beside 'fragment' and 'shelter'; it is the verb meaning criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is to criticise severely, and to denounce is to condemn publicly.

clue.text: Submission one's honoured to pass on by November (extremely close)

parts.note: the OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is an honour the recipient has received
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of close, its first and last, are used

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: Someone honoured is ready to submit, dying close to November.
explanation.walkthrough: N is November in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is the act of submitting to authority or another's will.

clue.text: Champ, taking lead in cross-country, fell

indicators.note: the lead, or opening letter, of cross-country is taken

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
to fell a tree is to hew it down

explanation.surface: A champion runner leading the cross-country race takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a champion; it is the verb meaning to munch noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch or chew noisily, as a horse champs its bit.

clue.text: Martinet succeeded overseeing trout fisherman?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece stands above, overseeing, the next one

parts.note: trout tickling is a way of catching fish by stroking their bellies by hand

explanation.surface: A strict boss took charge of supervising an angler.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on strict rules, just as a martinet is a strict disciplinarian.

clue.text: Arrows fired here resound, having swapped tips

indicators.note: the tips are the first and last letters, which change places

parts.note: to echo is to resound

explanation.surface: Archery language: a place where shots ring out.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two end letters change places. 'Arrows' is darts slang; the oche is the line players stand behind to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts, the player stands at the oche to throw, and darts are called arrows.

clue.text: Vessel for drinking tea shared with dreamy girl

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: the A that ends the tea also begins the girl, so the two pieces overlap by one letter

parts.note: Alice dreamt her adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A cup of tea split with a girl lost in daydreams.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a goblet, especially the cup used for wine at communion.

clue.text: Stylish lorry crosses first

indicators.note: the lorry's letters span across the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a semi-trailer truck
1st written in letters and digits, read as IST

explanation.surface: A smart-looking truck goes over the line in first place.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistic can mean showing aesthetic taste and flair, which is to say stylish.

clue.text: I reckon keeping step on Tango is an artform

indicators.note: the opinion holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: IMO is texting shorthand for 'in my opinion'

indicators.note: in a down clue the step sits on top of the next letter

parts.note: pas is a dance step, as in pas de deux

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a dance step in the tango counts as art.
explanation.walkthrough: T is Tango in the NATO alphabet; the dance is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a painting technique laying paint on thickly, so a method of creating art.

clue.text: Swansong less aloof

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a final act or number, the one that closes a show
second meaning: more intimate, comparative of close

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'doser', the other with 'dosser'.
explanation.definitionFit: A closer is a final performance piece, while closer also means more friendly and intimate.

clue.text: US road user from California leaves state then returns

parts.note: dill is a herb whose feathery leaves are used in cooking

indicators.note: the second abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: CA is the postal code for the state of California

explanation.surface: A US motorist from California leaves the state and later comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about departing; it is a noun, the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cadillac is a big American car, a road user in the sense of vehicle.

clue.text: Criminal boss claiming that chap's item of junk?

definitions.note: a cheapo is a cheap, shoddy thing; question mark since the word is also an adjective

indicators.note: the boss takes the other piece into his possession, inside him

parts.note: a capo is a Mafia boss
he is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A gangster lays claim to another man's worthless possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapo is a cheap, low-quality article, the sort of thing called rubbish.

clue.text: Pass through outskirts of Eswatini, a source of disease?

indicators.note: the pass goes through the middle of the other piece
only the outer letters of Eswatini are used

parts.note: the African kingdom, formerly Swaziland, whose two edge letters are used
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses the edges of Eswatini, an African country with health problems.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium whose harmful strains cause food poisoning.

clue.text: Liberace settled on this soft pair of slippers when entertaining excessively

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for playing softly

indicators.note: the opening pair hosts the other piece inside it

parts.note: the first pair of letters of slippers
too means excessively

explanation.surface: Liberace, flamboyant as ever, sat at home in comfy slippers putting on an over-the-top show.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberace was the flamboyant American pianist; settling on 'this' means sitting on it to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist like Liberace sits on a piano stool at the keyboard.

clue.text: Academic study held in circles roughly

indicators.note: the study sits inside the pair of circles

parts.note: two letters O look like circles
RS stands for Religious Studies, a school subject

explanation.surface: A university course conducted in vaguely circular fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Or so is tacked onto a number to mean approximately.

clue.text: The bed's displaying shrubby plant

indicators.note: the letters are on show within the words, spanning the gap

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A flower bed shows off a bushy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe is a genus of evergreen shrubs popular in gardens.

clue.text: Rovers footballer with rotund shape is performing singer

parts.note: Roy Race is the hero of the British comic strip Roy of the Rovers
an orb is a sphere
taken as written
a performer on stage is said to be on

explanation.surface: A rounded footballer from Rovers turns out to be a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Orbison was the American singer of 'Oh, Pretty Woman'.
